item.title: Gossip in Production Systems
item.description:
The previous four articles in this series built a complete knowledge foundation—from Epidemic propagation theory in Gossip, to the SWIM membership protocol, to P2P implementations in Rust and Go, and finally to production best practices. Now it is time to apply this knowledge to real distributed systems.

This article examines six representative systems and how they adapt Gossip protocols to different scenarios: from Gossipsub parameter tuning to Raft membership changes, from Redis Cluster PING/PONG to Cassandra’s GossipDigest protocol, and the hidden Gossip routing mechanisms inside message queues.

item.title: A Map of Distributed Consensus: From Paxos to DAG-BFT — Boundaries and Selection Across Four Families
item.description: etcd uses Raft, Cosmos uses Tendermint, Bitcoin uses PoW, Sui uses Mysticeti — they’re all “consensus,” but they do not solve the same problem. Electing a leader among a few known nodes in a datacenter and reaching agreement on a ledger among anonymous nodes on a public chain sit a full order of magnitude apart in their assumptions. Mashing every consensus algorithm onto one throughput axis is why so many selection guides read like mush.
